en.question: A team notices Claude Code repeatedly using the wrong test command for their project. What is the most durable fix?

options.text: Correct the command by hand at the start of each working session.
options.note: Unbounded repetition of the same correction, for every developer, forever.

options.text: Build an MCP server that exposes a run_tests tool with the right command.
options.note: Disproportionate, since the assistant can already run commands.

options.text: Record the canonical build and test commands in the project's CLAUDE.md.
Move the team onto a more capable model tier with better repo inference.
options.note: No model can guess a project-specific command it has never been told.

en.explanation: Repeated corrections are exactly what project memory is for: the knowledge becomes persistent, shared through version control, and loaded in every session.
